sections.name: File setup, TABS, Tab
sections.title: Imports and tab list
sections.what: Loads the React tools, the page navigation helper, the header and footer, and the profile functions. Also defines the eight tab names the editor shows.
sections.why: Defining the tabs once keeps the tab bar and the tab content in step.
sections.watch_out: A new tab must also have a matching content section in the page, or it will show nothing.

sections.name: Field
sections.title: Labeled field wrapper
sections.what: Puts a label above any input so each form field looks the same.
sections.why: Keeps label spacing and style consistent across the editor.

sections.name: inputStyle, taStyle, nanoid
sections.title: Shared input styles and random ids
sections.what: Holds the shared box styles for text inputs and text areas, and a helper that makes short random ids for new entries.
sections.why: Keeps the look consistent, and gives each new entry an id so it can be edited or removed.
sections.watch_out: Ids are short random strings with a small chance of two entries sharing one.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading the profile and autosave timer
sections.what: Loads the profile when the page opens and starts a 1.5 second countdown after each change, then saves and shows AUTO-SAVED briefly. Also defines the manual save and save-and-view actions.
sections.why: Saves work without the user pressing a button, which reduces lost edits.
sections.watch_out: Only the first load is skipped by autosave, so any later change, including one from seed data, is saved.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 2)
sections.title: Add, edit, remove, and reorder helpers
sections.what: Provides the actions to add, change, remove, and reorder roles, education, projects, certifications, and publications, plus the actions to rename, add, and remove skill categories.
sections.why: Keeps all list changes in one place, so each tab works the same way.
sections.watch_out: Moving or removing an entry takes effect at once and is autosaved, with no undo.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 3)
sections.title: Buttons and header bar
sections.what: Defines the button styles, including a red style for removal, and draws the header with the name, CANCEL, SAVE DRAFT, and SAVE and VIEW buttons, plus the tab bar.
sections.why: Keeps the main save actions in one fixed place so the user always knows how to save.
sections.watch_out: The SAVED message only shows briefly, so a user can miss it.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 4)
sections.title: Personal details tab
sections.what: Holds the name, years of experience, headline, primary and secondary email, phone, current location, open locations, and LinkedIn, GitHub, and portfolio links.
sections.why: Holds the basic identity details, and the headline label says it appears on resumes and cover letters.
sections.watch_out: Emails and links are free text and are not checked, so a typo is saved as typed.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 5)
sections.title: Work experience tab
sections.what: Lists each role with company, title, location, dates, a currently-here checkbox, and a box for bullet points. Users can add, reorder, and remove roles.
sections.why: The bullet box is the raw material for resume entries, as its label says.
sections.watch_out: The currently-here checkbox does not change the dates, so the user must update the date text by hand.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 6)
sections.title: Skills tab
sections.what: Shows one box per skill category with its comma-separated list and small tags previewing each skill. Users can rename, add, and remove categories.
sections.why: The page notes say these lists feed the resume and cover letter generators.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a category to a name already in use silently replaces that category's skills.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 7)
sections.title: Projects tab
sections.what: Lists projects with an internal name, optional repo link, description, tech stack, and outcomes, with reorder and remove actions.
sections.why: The page asks for capability descriptions, which give cover letters their proof points.
sections.watch_out: The repo link is free text and is not checked to exist.

sections.name: ProfileEditPage (part 8)
sections.title: Education tab
sections.what: Lists each school with institution, degree, field, GPA, years, and a box for notable work, and lets the user add or remove entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: a list lets the user add several degrees.
sections.watch_out: Education has no reorder buttons, unlike roles and projects, so entries stay in the order they were added.

summary: The full profile editor, with eight tabs where the user changes every part of the saved profile. Changes save automatically shortly after each edit.
purpose: Lets the user correct and add to their career details: identity, roles, skills, projects, education, certifications, publications, and voice notes.
why: Likely reason: one editor with autosave means work is rarely lost. Reason for the eight tabs not stated in the code.
how: 1. Loads the saved profile, or the seed profile if none exists. 2. Shows one tab at a time. 3. Each change updates the profile on screen. 4. About 1.5 seconds after the last change, the profile saves and an AUTO-SAVED note shows briefly. 5. SAVE DRAFT saves now, SAVE and VIEW saves and goes to the profile page, and CANCEL leaves without a new save, though earlier autosaves remain.
inputs: The saved profile from storage, or the seed profile if none is saved. Typed text and button clicks from the user.
outputs: The updated profile saved back to storage, and a SAVED or AUTO-SAVED message.
risks: Autosave saves whatever is on screen, so a removed entry is saved within about 1.5 seconds with no undo. Renaming a skill category to an existing name silently replaces that category's skills. If no profile exists, the seed sample data loads and the first edit saves it.
debug: If changes do not persist, check that the autosave timer runs and that saving is called. If unexpected sample data appears, check whether no profile was found and the seed fallback loaded. If a skill category disappears after a rename, check whether the new name matched an existing one.
